sections.html:
The Fayette County Recorder works from 133 S. Main Street, Suite 305, Washington Court House, Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4 pm. Phone 740-335-1770 or fax 740-333-3521. The office keeps all real estate and personal property records for the county, including:

  • deeds, mortgages and land contracts
  • IRS liens and mechanics liens
  • plats and zoning resolutions
  • military service discharges

Washington Court House is the county seat and the county's only city. Every deed for a Fayette County parcel is recorded at this one office, whether the house is in town or out in a township.

Fayette County charges a flat price by page count, and a one-page and a two-page deed cost the same.

Recording fee by document length
Pages in the documentRecording fee
1 page$39.00
2 pages$39.00
3 pages$47.00
4 pages$55.00
5 pages$63.00
10 pages$103.00

A $4.00 marginal fee can apply on top. Ask the office what a longer deed will cost, since the posted schedule stops at ten pages. Ohio Revised Code 317.32 builds these numbers from a base fee and a housing trust fund fee for each page, plus an optional document preservation surcharge of up to five dollars that the county may keep for its general fund.

sections.h2: Delivering a deed to the Recorder
sections.html:
Bring the deed to Suite 305 or mail it, and pay by cash or check. Credit and debit cards are not accepted.

  • Anything received after 3:30 PM is held and run the next day, so a late afternoon drop does not get that day's time stamp.
  • If you want papers mailed back, include a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
  • Since June 22, 2026, the county offers e-recording through Simplifile for both conveyance and non-conveyance documents.

The time stamp matters because Ohio recorders file instruments in order of presentation and note the exact time (R.C. 317.13). If two papers arrive for the same house, the earlier time gets priority.

sections.h2: What the Auditor does before the deed is recorded
sections.html:
A sale deed is presented to the Auditor's real estate department first. That office tracks deed transfers, new parcels, lot splits and homestead exemptions. It is at 133 S. Main Street, Suite 303, phone 740-335-6461, with the same Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm schedule.

The Auditor's forms page carries the conveyance papers: the Real Property Conveyance form (DTE 100), the Exemption from Real Property Conveyance form (DTE 100EX), a statement for homestead property, a statement for current agricultural use valuation property, and forms for mobile homes. The county also posts its conveyance standards for legal descriptions.

The DTE 100 asks for the total consideration and then the portion paid for items other than real property. The fee is figured on the real property consideration that remains. It also asks whether the seller said the home gets the senior or disabled homestead exemption or farm use valuation, and whether the buyer will live there by January 1 of the next year. Skipping the owner-occupancy application blocks that 2.5 percent reduction until a proper, timely application is filed, so fill that part in. Ask the Auditor for the current conveyance fee rate before closing.

An Ohio recorder may decline an instrument that is not required or authorized to be recorded, or that the recorder has reasonable cause to believe is materially false or fraudulent. Someone whose paper is turned away can ask the Court of Common Pleas to order recording.

One refusal is mandatory: a right-to-list home sale agreement described in R.C. 5301.94. If an owner is told such an agreement will be recorded against the house, the statute directs the recorder to turn it away.

The recorder has no duty to inspect or investigate what is handed over. Checking the legal description, names and signatures falls to whoever drafted the deed.

R.C. 317.32 sets several charges besides the recording fee, each split into a base fee and a housing trust fund fee of equal size:

  • Certified copy of a recorded document: $1 base plus $1 trust fund per page, with a further 50 cents plus 50 cents when the recorder's seal is required.
  • Photocopy outside the recording process: $1 plus $1 per page.
  • Marginal reference entered by a separate instrument: $2 plus $2 for each reference, which matches the $4.00 marginal fee Fayette posts.
  • Local fax or electronic transmission: $1 plus $1 per page.

A certified copy of your vesting deed is the extra sellers most often need, and a title company often asks for one.

sections.h2: Values, tax bills and a sale
sections.html:
The Auditor is the county's chief fiscal officer and its real property appraiser. Ohio directs a general reappraisal every six years, with an update in the third year. Each year the Auditor prepares the tax list, and after the Treasurer collects, the Auditor distributes the money to townships, schools and other taxing bodies. The Auditor also certifies and publishes the list of delinquent taxes, and the Treasurer then pursues those accounts.

The Auditor is secretary of the county Board of Revision, and the Board of Revision Property Complaint form is on the Auditor's forms page. If you dispute a value, use that form instead of taking the question to the Recorder. If the Auditor's online data for your parcel looks wrong, report it so the record can be corrected.

At the deed stage, state law requires the conveyance statement to confirm that the seller was asked whether the home gets a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction, and whether it was in farm use valuation. If farm use ends, a recoupment charge can follow, and buyer and seller account for it between themselves (R.C. 319.202). A seller of acreage that has been farmed should raise this with the title agent early.

Fayette County had 28,951 residents in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 28,552. Washington Court House anchors a micropolitan area that is part of the Columbus-Marion-Zanesville region, and the county borders Madison, Pickaway, Ross, Highland, Clinton and Greene counties. Good Hope and Pancoastburg are the named unincorporated places.

For a cash sale, plan the order of stops: legal description and conveyance forms at the Auditor in Suite 303, then the signed deed to the Recorder in Suite 305 before 3:30 PM. Bring a check or cash for the fee.

faqs.q: How much is the Fayette County recording fee for a two page deed?
faqs.a: $39.00, and the $4.00 marginal fee can apply on top. A one page deed is also $39.00, and three pages cost $47.00.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Fayette County Recorder by card?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder accepts cash or check only.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Fayette County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county offers e-recording through Simplifile for conveyance and non-conveyance documents. Paper filing at Suite 305 remains available.

faqs.q: What time should I get a deed to the Fayette County Recorder?
faqs.a: Before 3:30 PM. Documents received after that hour are held and run the following day.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County Recorder or Auditor handle the conveyance form?
faqs.a: The Auditor, at Suite 303 of the same building. The Real Property Conveyance form (DTE 100) and the exemption form (DTE 100EX) are on the Auditor's forms page, and the Recorder then files the deed.
